statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Current Tail risk remains in the low band.
recommendation: Current evidence supports a low Tail assessment while event stress remains elevated; the 10:00 ET U.S. data window is the nearest defined checkpoint.
headline: Low Tail risk despite elevated event and technology-sector stress
body: Overnight September NQ has retraced an early dip and is near flat, which does not show the persistent one-way structure required for a Tail block. Monday's technology weakness, Iran escalation risk, and the approaching U.S. data and Nvidia calendar keep Stress elevated. The principal near-term danger window is centered on the 10:00 ET Consumer Confidence and New Home Sales releases.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hours, published Tail moved from low to WATCH as Monday's technology-led selloff developed, briefly reached elevated at 18:00-19:00 UTC, then eased back through WATCH and returned to low after midnight. Stress remained extreme for most of Monday before dropping to the elevated band after 00:00 UTC.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are expected to remain event-sensitive but not automatically one-way. Tail is projected to stay low through Europe, rise into WATCH around the U.S. cash open and 10:00 ET Consumer Confidence/New Home Sales window, then ease if post-release price discovery is two-way. Wednesday's GDP, PCE, durable-goods and Nvidia events remain later checkpoints.

forecast.analysis: September NQ is near flat after an early overnight dip and rebound within a roughly 84-point range; that retracement argues against persistent one-way mean-reversion failure. Tech caution and Iran/Nvidia headlines keep Stress elevated.
drivers: Overnight NQ dip retraced toward the session high

news.title: Asia shares fall on tech nerves; oil prices slip
Iran vows to retaliate after US widens sanctions

forecast.analysis: Into 05:00 Berlin, risk remains conditional on whether the overnight rebound holds without renewed extension. With no major U.S. release in this hour, Tail stays low while cross-asset and geopolitical headlines preserve moderate-to-elevated Stress.
drivers: Overnight balance versus renewed directional break

forecast.analysis: Early European positioning can challenge the overnight balance. Tail remains low unless a fresh directional break develops with shallow pullbacks; otherwise the prior rebound and narrow overnight structure favor mixed rather than persistent trend risk.
drivers: Need for shallow/failed retracements before Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: At 07:00 Berlin, the base case is a quieter handoff before broader European liquidity. A clean two-way range would keep Tail low; a headline-driven break in oil, yields or tech futures would raise Stress before it justifies a Tail escalation.
drivers: Two-way range remains the base case

forecast.analysis: European pre-open liquidity begins to matter more. Tail stays low under a conditional two-way path, while Nvidia-event caution and Iran-related headline sensitivity keep Stress above a calm-session baseline.

news.title: Asia shares fall on tech nerves; oil prices slip

forecast.analysis: Ahead of the main European cash open, the key checkpoint is whether overnight balance survives the liquidity increase. Tail remains low unless directional efficiency rises and retracements become shallow or fail.
drivers: Retracement quality is the main Tail checkpoint

forecast.analysis: At the European cash open, mixed cross-asset reactions could widen intraday swings without creating a one-way NQ path. Stress edges up, while Tail remains low unless semiconductors and yields align with sustained futures extension.

One hour into Europe, the forecast assumes no confirmed persistent trend. Continued two-way trade would preserve low Tail; a synchronized move across NQ, semiconductors and yields would be the main conditional escalation signal.
drivers: NQ extreme-holding would be required for higher Tail

forecast.analysis: Late European morning can begin pricing the 10:00 ET U.S. releases. Stress rises modestly as event proximity increases, but Tail remains low because pre-release uncertainty is not evidence of failed mean reversion.

news.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq end down on tech stocks, investors weigh Iran moves

forecast.analysis: Approaching the U.S. premarket build, headline sensitivity increases around Iran, trade policy and Nvidia expectations. Tail remains low unless futures start holding near an extreme with repeated failed retracements.
At 14:00 Berlin, the U.S. premarket is more active and the 10:00 ET data window is two hours away. Stress moves into the high band, while Tail remains low absent a persistent directional price path.

From 09:00 ET, the final half-hour before the U.S. cash open raises opening-auction uncertainty, with the 10:00 ET data another hour away. Tail reaches WATCH only conditionally; persistent extension with weak retracement would be required to confirm it.

news.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq end down on tech stocks, investors weigh Iran moves

forecast.analysis: At 10:00 ET, after the first 30 minutes of cash trade, Consumer Confidence and New Home Sales create the day’s main whipsaw window. Tail is WATCH, not blocked, unless the opening and post-data path becomes persistently one-way with failed retracements.
drivers: First 30 minutes of U.S. cash trade
Consumer Confidence and New Home Sales at 10:00 ET

news.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq end down on tech stocks, investors weigh Iran moves

forecast.analysis: One hour after the 10:00 ET releases, Tail can ease if price discovery is two-way and retracements reappear. Stress remains high, while persistent extension, extreme-holding and aligned yields or semiconductors would keep Tail in WATCH.

Two hours after the releases, the base case shifts toward normalization. Tail remains WATCH at the margin but can fall to low if NQ shows normal pullbacks; continued yield and semiconductor alignment would delay that easing.

By early U.S. afternoon, event shock should be fading in the base case. Tail returns to low if NQ shows normal pullbacks; lingering yield, semiconductor or geopolitical alignment would be the main reason for continued caution.

Mid-afternoon risk is more path-dependent than event-dependent. A balanced session would keep Tail low and lower Stress, while sustained trend efficiency into the afternoon would invalidate that normalization.

Later U.S. afternoon normally offers more evidence on whether the morning move is durable. Tail stays low under a two-way session; repeated extension toward session extremes would be the key conditional escalation.
Entering the final two cash-market hours, Stress continues to ease in the base case. Tail remains low unless a late directional run develops with weak retracement and broad tech-sector confirmation.

During power-hour approach, liquidity and positioning can re-accelerate the day’s move. The forecast keeps Tail low unless NQ holds near an extreme and extends after failed pullbacks; generic late-session volatility alone is not enough.

At the U.S. cash close, a balanced finish would support normal conditions and low Tail. A close pinned near an extreme after repeated extension would instead leave more overnight continuation risk than this base case assumes.
drivers: Closing location within the session range

news.title: Iran vows to retaliate after US widens sanctions

forecast.analysis: Early post-close trade should be thinner and more headline-sensitive. Tail remains low if the cash-session move stabilizes; Iran developments or a sharp technology-sector repricing could raise Stress without automatically creating a block state.

At midnight Berlin, attention begins shifting toward Wednesday’s U.S. GDP, PCE and durable-goods releases. Those future events raise planning Stress modestly, but they do not count as observed Tail evidence in this hour.

Into the next Asian-session handoff, the next-day macro and Nvidia earnings calendar becomes more relevant. Tail stays low unless overnight futures develop sustained one-way structure; event proximity mainly lifts Stress rather than Tail.

forecastDetail.comment: Observed overnight dip-and-rebound structure argues against immediate one-way Tail behavior; event and tech headlines keep Stress elevated.
Absent a fresh break, the early-morning base case remains mixed with low Tail and slowly easing Stress.
European liquidity is the next structural test; higher Tail would require sustained extension with weak retracement.
Before broader Europe opens, headline risk can lift Stress without proving persistent directional failure.
Pre-open positioning may widen moves, but Tail stays low unless semiconductors, yields and NQ align directionally.
The European cash-open approach is a checkpoint for whether the overnight balance survives stronger liquidity.
